title: Load Test Campaign (Candidate)
description: Candidate decision-first dashboard. It separates historical observation coverage from steady-state throughput and keeps workload-specific diagnostics collapsed. Loadgen and Kubernetes panels are scoped by loadgen job, namespace, and pod; service-side panels follow their metric contract labels and assume the selected per-site Prometheus datasource represents one site.

list.name: target_rps
list.label: Target RPS
list.description: Fallback rate for message, member, and bot-room commands. Soak mode uses the aggregate loadgen_soak_configured_rate exported by loadgen when that telemetry exists.

list.name: loadgen_job
list.label: Loadgen scrape job
list.description: Prometheus scrape job that exports loadgen_* metrics. Runtime process/go panels use the same job so local exporter processes cannot be mistaken for loadgen.

list.name: namespace
list.label: Namespace
list.description: Namespace the loadgen pod runs in. Every panel is scoped to it, including the kube-state joins for memory and CPU limits, which key on namespace and pod. All is the default and also the only working value outside Kubernetes -- the repo's local docker-compose stack emits no namespace label, and the selector matches series that lack it.

list.name: pod
list.label: Pod name filter
list.description: Regex matched against the pod name. The default .* also matches the bundled local scrape, whose series have no pod label; the loadgen job selector still excludes exporter processes. Narrow it to one pod name to isolate a single Kubernetes loadgen process.

panels.title: How to read this campaign
panels.description: Start with whether the selected window was observed, then verify steady-state load, impact, latency, errors, backlog, and recovery. Workload-specific diagnostics stay collapsed.

options.content:
### Read left to right
1. **Observation coverage** should be at least 95% for the selected window.
2. **Steady-state attainment** should be at least 95%; startup and shutdown tails are intentionally excluded by the median.
3. **SOAK ONLY / NOT APPLICABLE** is expected for soak panels outside soak mode.
4. **KUBERNETES METRIC UNAVAILABLE** is expected for Kubernetes-only panels in local Docker.
5. Error panels show an explicit zero only when matching traffic or telemetry was observed; otherwise they remain **UNKNOWN**.
6. Check **pipeline, failures, latency, backlog, and recovery**, then open collapsed rows only for diagnosis.

Soak mode uses loadgen's exported aggregate configured rate. For message, member, and bot-room modes, set **Target RPS** to the rate passed to loadgen. Status cards summarize the selected Prometheus window, not the state after loadgen stopped. Exact completed-run totals remain in the loadgen CLI summary.

panels.title: Observation coverage
panels.description: Average scrape health across the selected historical window while loadgen metrics were observable. Unlike a point-in-time freshness check, stopping loadgen after a successful run does not turn the whole campaign into UNKNOWN.

panels.title: Steady-state target attainment
panels.description: Median achieved rate across the selected window divided by the median configured soak rate when soak telemetry exists, otherwise Target RPS. The median represents sustained load and avoids treating startup or shutdown tail samples as the campaign result. Exact whole-run totals remain in the CLI summary.

targets.expr: 100 * quantile_over_time(0.5, (((sum(rate(loadgen_soak_lane_attempts_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod",outcome="sent"}[$__rate_interval]))) or sum(rate(loadgen_published_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod",phase="measured"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum(rate(loadgen_member_published_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod",phase="measured"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum(rate(loadgen_botroom_published_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod",phase="measured"}[$__rate_interval]))))[$__range:$__interval]) / (quantile_over_time(0.5, (sum(loadgen_soak_configured_rate{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}))[$__range:$__interval]) or vector($target_rps))

panels.title: Target vs achieved throughput
panels.description: Target and observed send/publish rate. Startup and shutdown tails remain visible for diagnosis; use Steady-state target attainment above for the campaign-level throughput decision.

panels.title: Service pipeline throughput
panels.description: Service-side processing rates. These counters are attempts/outcomes, not a strict loss-proof funnel: redelivery and fan-out can make stages differ. Use the shape to locate where throughput stops keeping up, then confirm with backlog and terminal failures.

panels.title: Service-side terminal failures
panels.description: Production-side work that will receive no further application attempt, grouped by service, consumer, and reason. The explicit zero is fail-closed: it appears only while accepted, persisted, broadcast-delivered, and notification-sent traffic are all observed. Other campaign modes remain PIPELINE NOT OBSERVED rather than claiming a healthy zero.

targets.expr: sum by (service_name, consumer, reason) (rate(chat_nats_terminal_failures_total[$__rate_interval])) or on() (0 * ((sum(rate(message_gatekeeper_messages_total{result="accepted"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0) and on() (sum(rate(message_worker_persistence_total{result="success"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0) and on() (sum(rate(broadcast_worker_recipient_deliveries_total{result="success"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0) and on() (sum(rate(notification_worker_outcomes_total{result="sent"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)))

panels.title: User-visible latency
panels.description: User-visible latency from loadgen histograms. Prometheus histogram quantiles are bucket estimates, so the loadgen CLI summary remains the exact completed-run percentile source.

panels.title: Errors and retries
panels.description: Error and retry rates. Each zero baseline is emitted only when its corresponding traffic series is observed; otherwise the panel remains UNKNOWN rather than claiming a healthy zero.

targets.expr: sum by (action) (rate(loadgen_soak_retries_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod",phase="measured"}[$__rate_interval])) or on (action) (0 * sum by (action) (rate(loadgen_soak_operations_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod",phase="measured"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Consumer backlog and drain
panels.description: JetStream messages not yet delivered to each durable. Growth during traffic can be normal; a plateau or continued growth after load stops means the consumer is not catching up. This exporter-backed view works for every workload.

panels.title: Recovery: operations still in flight
panels.description: A recovery view, not just a load view. Fault-ledger operations and JetStream pending/in-flight work should return to baseline after traffic or fault injection stops. If the selected window ends first, recovery is unconfirmed.

panels.title: Soak run identity (selected window)
panels.description: Bounded run metadata published only in soak mode. SOAK ONLY / NOT APPLICABLE is expected for message, member, and bot-room campaigns. During a soak campaign, an empty result means loadgen was not scraped and all soak evidence is unreliable.

panels.title: OOM-killed loadgen containers (Kubernetes only)
panels.description: kube-state-metrics last-terminated reason for loadgen pods. Any non-zero value means a loadgen container was OOM-killed and the run is suspect. KUBERNETES METRIC UNAVAILABLE is expected in local Docker and does not prove that there were no OOM kills.

targets.expr: sum(kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod",reason="OOMKilled"} and on (namespace, pod) count by (namespace, pod) (process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$loadgen_job"}))

panels.title: Loadgen memory limit utilization (Kubernetes only)
panels.description: RSS as a percentage of the Kubernetes container memory limit. KUBERNETES METRIC UNAVAILABLE is expected in local Docker; use the absolute RSS and Go heap panel instead. In Kubernetes, an empty result means kube resource-limit labels cannot be joined and must not be read as 0%.

targets.expr: 100 * process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$loadgen_job", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} / on (namespace, pod) group_left() sum by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod",resource="memory"})

panels.title: Loadgen memory: RSS, Go heap, next GC
panels.description: RSS is what the OOM killer sees. The gap between RSS and heap-in-use is off-heap: cgo, mmap'd WAL pages, and the runtime's own arenas -- invisible to go_memstats_*. A rising gap with a flat heap is the shape that preceded the earlier loadgen OOMs.

panels.title: Loadgen CPU: used vs limit
panels.description: Cores consumed against the container CPU limit. Loadgen is an open-loop generator: once it is CPU-saturated it stops being able to offer the configured rate, and the scheduler-underrun series in the throughput row will rise at the same time. Read the two together before blaming the system under test.

panels.title: Loadgen runtime: goroutines and open files
panels.description: A goroutine count that climbs and never returns is a leak in a lane; open file descriptors climbing is usually leaked connections or unclosed WAL segments. Both precede an OOM.

panels.title: Loadgen NATS connection (selected window)
panels.description: Worst connection state observed for each loadgen pool in the selected window. DISCONNECTED during an intentional NATS fault can be expected; outside that window it makes in-flight evidence unreliable. UNKNOWN means no connection telemetry was observed in the selected window.

panels.title: Failure observers (selected window)
panels.description: Worst asynchronous failure-observer state in the selected soak window. DOWN means affected operations can resolve only as unverified. SOAK ONLY / NOT APPLICABLE is expected for campaigns that do not start failure observers.

panels.title: Soak evidence ledger: WAL durability
panels.description: p99 of the grouped fsync barrier, failed append rate, mean group-commit batch size, and evidence-sidecar write rate. The ledger is the only record of what was intended; if appends error or the barrier stalls, operations are lost from the ledger and the campaign is INCONCLUSIVE rather than clean. Correlate latency with batch size before attributing dispatch shortfall to the system under test.

targets.expr: sum by (result) (rate(loadgen_failure_wal_flush_batch_size_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (result) (rate(loadgen_failure_wal_flush_batch_size_count{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.000000001)

panels.title: Soak evidence invalidations by reason
panels.description: Every condition that makes this campaign's evidence INCONCLUSIVE, by bounded reason. Any bar here means the Evidence tile at the top of the dashboard should be read as INCONCLUSIVE regardless of what the Impact tile says.

panels.title: Soak ledger WAL size and abandoned journals
panels.description: WAL bytes on disk and journals retained from an earlier ledger epoch that will never be replayed. A growing WAL with no drain is what precedes the capacity invalidation; abandoned journals mean operations from a previous process are permanently unresolvable.

panels.title: Soak control plane (selected window)
panels.description: Worst Mongo-primary reachability and manifest-heartbeat state observed in the selected soak window. SOAK ONLY / NOT APPLICABLE is expected for other campaign modes. During soak, an empty result means the control plane was not observed.

panels.title: Soak control-plane freshness and attempts
panels.description: Seconds since the latest successful manifest heartbeat and latest completed Mongo primary Ping, plus both probes' attempt outcomes. A staleness line that climbs without resetting means the corresponding control-plane evidence is frozen; a recovered error counter preserves failures that occurred between scrapes.

targets.expr: ((time() - loadgen_soak_heartbeat_success_timestamp_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) and loadgen_soak_heartbeat_success_timestamp_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} > 0) and on() max(max_over_time(loadgen_run_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range]))

sum by (outcome) (increase(loadgen_soak_heartbeat_attempts_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) and on() max(max_over_time(loadgen_run_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range]))

((time() - loadgen_mongo_probe_timestamp_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) and loadgen_mongo_probe_timestamp_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} > 0) and on() max(max_over_time(loadgen_run_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range]))

sum by (outcome) (increase(loadgen_mongo_probe_attempts_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod",outcome="error"}[2m])) and on() max(max_over_time(loadgen_run_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Soak ledger accounting gaps
panels.description: untracked (by reason start/observe/abandon) means loadgen could not even record what happened; dropped means recovered operations were discarded at startup because the journal exceeded capacity. Both are strictly worse than bad: the outcome is unknown and unknowable.

targets.expr: sum by (reason) (increase(loadgen_failure_untracked_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) and on() max(max_over_time(loadgen_run_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Soak observer validity and queue pressure
panels.description: Numerator and denominator of the failure-evidence observer contract, plus the live observer queue depth on the right axis. The interval is invalid when unverified exceeds max(3, ceil(0.001 * eligible)) for a lane and observer. Queue depth should repeatedly drain to zero; sustained growth means the observer is alive but falling behind. A disabled observer is not eligible; NO DATA remains inconclusive.

targets.expr: max by (observer) (loadgen_failure_observer_queue_depth{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) and on() max(max_over_time(loadgen_run_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Soak reconcile capacity and lag
panels.description: Validity gate for fault windows. A sustained zero idle-claim rate means the reconciler has no spare capacity; p99 lag approaching SOAK_RECONCILE_DEADLINE means operations can expire unverified for want of a probe. Any reconcile_capacity, reconcile_lag_range, or lease_abort invalidation makes the affected interval INCONCLUSIVE.

targets.expr: sum by (outcome) (rate(loadgen_failure_reconcile_claims_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) and on() max(max_over_time(loadgen_run_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range]))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(loadgen_failure_reconcile_lag_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on() max(max_over_time(loadgen_run_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Evidence validity blockers
panels.description: Soak/failure only. Any non-zero value makes the affected evidence window INCONCLUSIVE. Zero is meaningful only while Telemetry is LIVE and traffic attainment is valid.

panels.title: Unrecovered impact
panels.description: Soak/failure only. Operations observed wrong or still missing after their deadline. A positive value is impact even if another evidence source is unavailable.

panels.title: Correctness violations
panels.description: Soak/failure only. Read-back results that were missing, mismatched, or malformed. RPC availability errors are shown separately in Errors and retries.

panels.title: Terminal operation results
panels.description: Every fault-observation operation resolves to exactly one terminal result: good (observed correct), bad (observed wrong), unverified (no observer could decide), not_sent (proven never to have left loadgen), missing_after_deadline (never observed in time). not_sent is not loss -- it is proof the system was never asked. bad and missing_after_deadline are.

panels.title: Unrecovered operations by scenario and lane
panels.description: Where the loss landed. Empty means no operation in range finished bad or missing_after_deadline; it does not mean traffic was offered -- confirm that in the throughput row first.

panels.title: Read-back violations by action and field
panels.description: Soak wrote something, read it back, and the two disagreed. field names the column that differed. class=missing means the write is not there at all; mismatch means it is there with the wrong value; malformed means it could not be parsed. retryable_rpc and rpc_error are excluded here -- they are availability, not correctness.

panels.title: Observation reasons
panels.description: The bounded reason behind each observation result -- this is where a search_index poison-ack or a room_state source disagreement shows up as a named cause rather than a bare unverified.

targets.expr: topk(25, sum by (scenario, lane, observer, result, reason) (increase(loadgen_failure_observation_reasons_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Mutation targets missing
panels.description: Soak mutations whose target row was still absent after the dedicated retry policy. Non-zero means a write soak believed it had made is not readable -- count it as loss, not as a slow read.

panels.title: Encryption preflight
panels.description: 1 once this run proved a message reached Cassandra encrypted with the room DEK wrapped. 0 means not proven: skipped by configuration, still in flight, failed, or a loadgen mode that never runs the check. Treat a sustained 0 during a soak run as a finding, not any single 0.

panels.title: Operations recovered from the ledger
panels.description: Unresolved operations replayed from the persistent WAL at startup. Non-zero means loadgen restarted mid-campaign; correlate with the OOM tile above before trusting any before/after comparison across that point.

panels.title: Proven not-sent by lane and reason
panels.description: Operations loadgen can prove never reached the network, split by lane. These are deliberately excluded from impact; a lane that is mostly not_sent is offering far less load than the pacing table's dispatched column suggests.

panels.title: Soak lane dispatch deficit
panels.description: Fraction of intended pacing events a lane did not dispatch. A lane with no intent in range is absent rather than 0% -- the ratio is undefined, and showing it as 0 would read as a healthy lane that is in fact not running at all.

panels.title: Soak per-lane pacing (all 14 lanes)
panels.description: One row per soak lane, so a lane that has silently stopped is visible as an empty row rather than as a missing line in a 14-series chart. sent, no_target and refused come from loadgen_soak_lane_attempts_total: dispatched counts scheduler slots, which a lane with an exhausted target pool still consumes, so only sent is offered load. underrun means the scheduler was too late to dispatch; lane sat / global sat mean the in-flight budget was full.

panels.title: Soak operations by outcome
panels.description: Measured-phase operations only (phase="measured"; warmup is excluded because its rates say nothing about steady-state behaviour). skipped is loadgen declining to act, not a system failure.

panels.title: Publish rates by generator
panels.description: The non-soak generators. Each is only present in the loadgen mode that runs it, so an absent series here means that mode was not used, not that publishing stopped.

panels.title: Soak member candidate pool and room budget
panels.description: Candidates by lifecycle state, the rooms the create lane may still add, and whether the pool is currently degraded. A degraded pool is reversible and clears on its own; what matters is a lane showing no_target in the pacing table at the same time.

panels.title: Soak presence lane
panels.description: Virtual connections by the status the lane last asked for, the rate of published presence signals, and the result of each presence query comparison. A presence publish is unacknowledged and is never on its own evidence the server saw it -- only the check results are.

panels.title: Soak room state observer sources
panels.description: Which source answered each room-state observation and how it turned out. A shift in source mix during a fault window changes what the room_state observer is actually proving, so read it before trusting that observer's verdicts.

panels.title: Soak RPC latency
panels.description: All soak actions together. Percentiles from Prometheus histograms are diagnostic only: they are interpolated within a bucket and aggregated across pods, so use them to see shape and movement, never as a pass/fail threshold for a campaign.

panels.title: Soak RPC latency by action
panels.description: One row per action so a single slow action is readable at a glance. The top histogram bucket is 5s: an action whose real latency exceeds that reports at the bucket edge, so a p99 pinned near 5s means "at least 5s", not "5s".

panels.title: Message path latency (E1 / E2)
panels.description: E1 is the gatekeeper ack; E2 is publish until the message is broadcast-visible. E2 minus E1 is the canonical-stream fan-out. Present only in message mode.

panels.title: Member-add latency (E1 / E2)
panels.description: E1 is the room-service reply; E2 is publish until room-worker emits the RoomMemberEvent, which reflects room-worker's ROOMS consumer throughput rather than any broadcast fan-out. A rising E2 with a flat E1 points at the ROOMS durable in the backlog row.

panels.title: Bot-room latency by room size
panels.description: Publish-to-broadcast and room-service read latency bucketed by room size. This is the fan-out cost curve: if p95 grows with size, the cost is per recipient.

panels.title: Soak evidence durability latency
panels.description: The cost loadgen pays to record evidence: WAL append, the grouped fsync barrier, and the recipient sidecar flush. When these rise, measured latency above includes loadgen's own disk, so check here before attributing a regression to the system under test.

panels.title: Soak error reasons
panels.description: The service-supplied reason behind each error class. This is the panel that turns "internal errors are up" into a named cause you can hand to a service owner.

targets.expr: topk(25, sum by (action, class, reason) (increase(loadgen_soak_error_reasons_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod",phase="measured"}[$__range]))) or on() (0 * max(max_over_time(loadgen_run_info{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Publish-side errors by reason
panels.description: Errors on the way out of loadgen, across the message, member and bot-room generators. saturated and underrun are loadgen's own back-pressure, not system failures -- read them together with the pacing table.

targets.expr: sum by (reason) (rate(loadgen_publish_errors_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() (0 * sum(rate(loadgen_published_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum by (reason) (rate(loadgen_member_publish_errors_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() (0 * sum(rate(loadgen_member_published_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum by (reason) (rate(loadgen_botroom_publish_errors_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) or on() (0 * sum(rate(loadgen_botroom_published_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Soak target pool pressure
panels.description: Mutations skipped for lack of a usable target, and the result of re-probing quarantined candidates. Sustained exhaustion means the pool never recovers and the affected lanes are offering no load at all.

panels.title: Loadgen NATS outage duration
panels.description: p95 and p99 of completed disconnections per pool, plus the duration of any outage still in progress. Short reconnects during an injected NATS fault are expected; a growing current-outage line means loadgen remains disconnected and the completed-outage histogram cannot yet describe it.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, pool) (rate(loadgen_nats_outage_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))) or on (pool) (0 * max by (pool) (max_over_time(loadgen_nats_connected{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, pool) (rate(loadgen_nats_outage_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))) or on (pool) (0 * max by (pool) (max_over_time(loadgen_nats_connected{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))
max by (pool) (loadgen_nats_current_outage_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) or on (pool) (0 * max by (pool) (loadgen_nats_connected{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}))

panels.title: Consumer telemetry (selected window)
panels.description: Worst telemetry availability, last pending value, and peak in-flight, redelivery, and stall values for each durable in the selected window. AVAILABLE THROUGHOUT means the sampler stayed readable; backlog columns determine whether the consumer kept up.

targets.expr: max by (durable) (max_over_time(loadgen_consumer_ack_floor_stall_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])) or on (durable) (-1 + 0 * max by (durable) (max_over_time(loadgen_consumer_up{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Ack floor stall by durable
panels.description: Seconds since the ack floor last advanced while work remained pending. Unlike pending, this cannot be explained by a burst of new traffic: any sustained climb means the durable is not acknowledging.

panels.title: Ack pending and redelivered by durable
panels.description: ack pending is in-flight work; on a FIFO lane with MaxAckPending=1 it is capped at 1 by design and a value of 1 is not a problem. redelivered climbing means messages are being retried, which with MaxDeliver=-1 can continue indefinitely.

panels.title: Consumer sampling errors
panels.description: Why the sampler could not read a durable. Any rate here means the backlog panels above are missing data for that durable -- absence of a series is a sampling failure, never a zero backlog.

targets.expr: sum by (durable, reason) (increase(loadgen_consumer_sample_errors_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) or on (durable) (0 * max by (durable) (max_over_time(loadgen_consumer_up{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))
